Parent #1926 (SC-03, SC-08) / #1645 (SC-10 route-switch element). Scoped child adding the browser-level route-switch witness.

## Requirements: A live route switch keeps the renderer and its stream

#2126 proves P2P and Relay observe one Agent stream timeline, and #2129 proves a forced route flip revokes the parser-applied cursor. What is missing is the **live route change the product actually performs**.

Corrected after reading the attach flow (2026-10-21): the UI has no live manual route switch. The session-row gear opens the attach dialog in `configure` intent, whose only action is **Save** — it persists the mode for the *next* attach. Clicking the row of the already-attached, healthy Session is deliberately a no-op (`requestAttach`), and a **manual** P2P route that disconnects ends in `transport-exhausted` (manualRoute), not a Relay fallback (`AddressAttachPolicy.onCandidateDisconnected`). The live P2P→Relay change is the **Auto** route's policy: when its P2P candidates are gone, it calls `force-relay` and re-attaches over Relay without tearing down the renderer.

The fixture must therefore:

- attach a Session in **Auto** mode (effective route P2P) and mark the current xterm DOM node;
- print a pre-switch marker and wait for it exactly once;
- make the P2P transport deterministically fail (suppress the liveness probe's `control.ping`; the runtime's 5 s deadline declares the candidate gone), letting the Auto policy rotate through its candidates and reach `force-relay`;
- assert the same xterm node survives, the pre-switch marker still occurs exactly once, and a post-switch marker arrives exactly once over the Relay route;
- start a numbered burst before/while the switch happens and prove its retained tail is exactly once (no duplicate, no missing line).

A manual switch back to P2P is **not** part of this fixture: the product only applies a manual mode on the next attach, and whether that flow keeps the renderer is a separate product question. Degraded-vs-synchronized surfacing is out of scope (tracked by #2155).

## Success Criteria

- [ ] SC-01 An Auto-route P2P transport failure falls back to Relay without remounting the xterm; the pre-switch marker remains exactly once and a post-switch marker arrives exactly once.
- [ ] SC-02 A numbered burst spanning the fallback has an exactly-once retained tail on the Relay route, and the controller can still write afterwards.
- [ ] SC-03 Exact PR HEAD Quality / E2E / Case Smoke / trusted Acceptance, and exact merge-SHA Quality / E2E / Cases / Orchestrator Pass.
